security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI M-mode trap handler or HSM context-save/restore code reads mcsps, masks off bits [3:2] as WPRI per the pre-787 spec, then writes the masked value back to mcsps on hardware implementing the new spec (where bits [3:2] are part of the SP field, SP[XLEN-1:2])
security_spec.summary: mcsps SP field widened from XLEN-1:4 to XLEN-1:2 (former WPRI bits 3:2 now hold SP data); OpenSBI CSR save/restore that zeros bits 3:2 as WPRI will truncate the M-mode shadow stack pointer, causing misaligned-stack corruption on mret after SBI call handling or HSM resume

findings.finding: OpenSBI does not define CSR_MSPCS (0x349) and has zero references to the mcsps/mspcs CSR anywhere in the codebase. No trap handler code, HSM save/restore code, or platform init code reads, modifies, or writes the mcsps CSR. The reported vulnerability pattern (reading mcsps, masking bits [3:2] as WPRI per pre-787 spec, and writing back on post-787 hardware where bits [3:2] are part of SP[XLEN-1:2]) cannot be triggered because OpenSBI never touches this CSR. The Smcsps extension CSR interaction is simply not implemented yet.
findings.snippet: No mcsps/mspcs/0x349 reference anywhere in the codebase.

spec_citations.excerpt: (NEW) 0x349   mspcs        M-mode stack pointer for conditional swap (WARL)
mspcs.PPUSH = mspcs.PUSH; if (mspcs.PUSH == 1) { rd = mspcs.SP; mspcs.SP = tmp[XLEN-1:4]; mspcs.PUSH = 0; }
